title: Bitcoin and the first cryptocurrency
summary: Bitcoin was set out in a white paper by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto dated 31 October 2008, and the network began in 2009. Its project describes it as the first decentralized peer-to-peer payment network, with no central authority. Mining paid 50 bitcoins per block at first, halving every 210,000 blocks toward a 21-million-coin limit reached around 2140.

uncertainty.note: Start is the date printed on the white paper (31 October 2008). End is the year the network began: bitcoin.org dates the first specification and proof of concept to 2009, Cambridge's index dates the network's inception to 2009, and the genesis block carries Unix time 1231006505 (3 January 2009, 18:15:05 UTC).

importance.justification: Bitcoin is the first decentralized cryptocurrency; its 2009 launch turned the white paper's peer-to-peer cash design into a working global network whose energy use is now measured by a university research centre.

beats.caption: Satoshi Nakamoto publishes the white paper Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System, dated 31 October 2008.
The network begins in 2009, paying miners 50 bitcoins per block on a schedule that ends around 2140.
